Score specification (S3) for U-stat kernels

Source: R/api-scores.R
new_score.Rd

A score (kernel) is a symmetric function evaluated on s-sized subsets. Provide either ptr (compiled fast path), or an R eval_batch, or an R eval.

Usage

new_score(
  name,
  order,
  setup = NULL,
  eval = NULL,
  eval_batch = NULL,
  eval_param = NULL,
  eval_param_batch = NULL,
  grad = NULL,
  grad_batch = NULL,
  fd_step = 1e-06,
  fd_scheme = "central",
  ptr = NULL,
  randomized = FALSE,
  symmetric = TRUE
)

Arguments

name

Character scalar.

order

Integer order s, or function(n, data, ctx) -> s.

setup

Optional function(data, ...) -> ctx object (list or externalptr).

eval

R fallback: function(idxs, data, ctx, rng) -> numeric(1).

eval_batch

R fast path: function(subs, data, ctx, rng) -> numeric(nrow(subs)).

eval_param

Optional parameter-aware scalar evaluator: function(idxs, data, theta, ctx, rng) -> numeric(1).

eval_param_batch

Optional parameter-aware batch evaluator: function(subs, data, theta, ctx, rng) -> numeric(nrow(subs)).

grad

Optional analytic scalar gradient: function(idxs, data, theta, ctx, rng) -> numeric(length(theta)).

grad_batch

Optional analytic batch gradient: function(subs, data, theta, ctx, rng) -> matrix(nrow(subs), length(theta)).

fd_step

Finite-difference step used by score_diff_path() when method = "fd" and no explicit step is supplied.

fd_scheme

Finite-difference scheme used by score_diff_path() when method = "fd" and no explicit scheme is supplied. One of c("central", "forward").

ptr

External pointer to compiled score (see vignette); if present, used by engine.

randomized

Logical: does the kernel draw randomness?

symmetric

Logical: permutation symmetry (engine assumes TRUE).

Value

An object of class ustat_score.

Details

If your score depends on a parameter vector (for example Z-estimation), use eval_param/eval_param_batch and optionally grad/grad_batch to enable derivative-aware workflows via score_diff_path().

See also

as_score(), score_eval(), score_eval_batch(), score_diff_path()

Examples

sc <- new_score(
  name = "sum2",
  order = 2L,
  eval = function(idxs, data, ctx, rng) sum(data[idxs])
)
is_score(sc)
#> [1] TRUE
